chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Burayd and Yunus ibn Dhabyan, they said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about a man who enters into ihram in Rajab or in the month of Ramadan, so when the time for Hajj comes, he performs Tamattu', so he said: 'There is no harm in that.'

And those upon whom Tamattu' is not obligatory are the people of Mecca, or whoever whose home is before the Miqat to Mecca, or if there is between him and Mecca forty-eight miles, then it is not permissible for them to perform Tamattu'. That is indicated by what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ مِيلًا: Forty-eight miles (a specific distance defining the boundary for exemption)
key_terms.إِحْرَام: Entering the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.التَّمَتُّع: The form of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, exits ihram, and then re-enters for Hajj
key_terms.الْمَوَاقِيت: Designated stations/places where pilgrims enter ihram
key_terms.رَجَب: The seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.رَمَضَان: The ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّع: One who performs Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from the obligation of performing Tamattu' in Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of entering *Ihram* early in months like Rajab or Ramadan, confirming that such pilgrims may validly perform *Tamattu'* by performing *Umrah* first and then *Hajj*. It further delineates the obligation of *Tamattu'* for travelers from beyond the *Miqat* boundaries (specifically those residing more than forty-eight miles from Mecca), while exempting residents of Mecca and those within that radius, reflecting the juristic consensus on the geographical scope of this ritual form.
